description: Trigger: apps/gateway/src/request_payloads.rs:132 defaults payload capture to true; capture() buffers up to 1 MiB of request bytes (142-190) and tees the response stream into another 1 MiB buffer, then writes to storage through a global semaphore of 4 (request_payloads.rs:15). request_timings.rs:104-150 writes a timing row per attempt through another semaphore of 4. description: Revalidated 2026-10-29 at 87640992. migration_compatibility.rs reconstructs migrations 1..=383 from markers in 0001_initial_schema.sql, runs them with SQLx's advisory lock, then separately DELETEs receipts 1..=383 and INSERTs the v1 baseline. (1) Two gateways starting during the upgrade can both pass the pre-collapse check; one collapses, the other then hits a checksum mismatch or a v1 primary-key conflict and fails startup (transient crash, no data corruption). notes:
2026-11-13 08:05 UTC admin-route review: gateway logs reported durable storage pool_timeout and 503 on model/currency requests and readiness; browser subsequently observed HTTP 502 and transient login redirect while /readyz also returned 502. Render reported the staging core PostgreSQL service available. A subsequent direct readiness request returned 200. Connection-pool exhaustion or database unavailability is not distinguished by this evidence; do not conflate this with mock-payment psycopg idle connection issue niu-fc72. Sustained recovery and root cause remain unverified.
2026-11-13 hosted candidate 101412e7: Credits briefly reported online top-ups unavailable, then exposed Add credits after current order status refresh. Mock gateway configuration showed enabled and the existing pending order remained readable. External read-only database connection was unavailable and Render CLI SSH required interactive mode in this environment; pool timeout root cause remains unverified. Avoid conflating payment gateway enabled with actual availability.
2026-11-13 follow-up: Render reports no external IP allowlist entries for the staging core PostgreSQL service, and an external read-only connection closes during TLS. Interactive Render CLI located the live instance but SSH preparation returned service not found for the staging service. No access configuration was changed. Connection-pool root cause and a safe internal database observation remain unverified.
2026-11-13 08:35:42 UTC: staging core PostgreSQL logs show statement timeout on SQL whose public source lines match enrich_key_views in crates/storage/src/keys.rs. Gateway logs at the same timestamp record SQLSTATE 57014 for a keys request and HTTP 503. This directly identifies one key-loading failure as a bounded query timeout, distinct from earlier pool-acquisition timeouts; it does not establish why the query was slow or that it caused pool exhaustion. Query plans and a safe current-data reproduction remain unavailable without internal database access. No query or financial semantics changed.
2026-11-13 further diagnosis: CLI service-not-found was caused by the CLI selecting a different workspace. In an isolated temporary CLI configuration selecting Niu, Render found the live staging instance, but SSH authentication returned Permission denied (publickey). The original CLI workspace remained unchanged; no SSH key or network allowlist was modified. Internal current-data query plan remains unavailable.
2026-11-13 database log correlation: at 08:04:21 UTC PostgreSQL reported an interrupted database system, at 08:04:26 automatic recovery, and at 08:04:28 readiness to accept connections. Connection-reset and statement-timeout messages followed in the fetched 08:04–08:07 interval, which overlaps the separately observed gateway pool timeouts. This is a concrete database interruption near that failure period, not proof of the interruption cause or of every 503. After the 08:44 deployment, the fetched database log window contained no statement-timeout, connection-limit or deadlock messages; absence in that limited window does not establish sustained recovery.
2026-11-13 database log detail: at 08:04:20 UTC PostgreSQL reported that a server process was terminated by signal 9, followed by termination of other active server processes; the database reported interruption and automatic recovery. The log does not identify the sender or establish an out-of-memory cause. Gateway pool failures followed in the same incident window; causation for every error remains unverified.
2026-11-13 at 11:49:04 UTC a second PostgreSQL server process was terminated by signal 9; PostgreSQL terminated other processes, reported interruption, ran automatic recovery and became ready at 11:49:10, followed by connection resets. This confirms recurrence, but the logs do not establish signal origin, out-of-memory, or common root cause with the earlier failure. The earlier failed process was executing a credential-validation read at termination; a running query alone does not prove it caused termination. No credentials or query values recorded.

close_reason: Rejected as contrary to the documented required-input detector privacy design. docs/releases/required-input-detector-verification.md requires explicit external-processing consent, a versioned processing fingerprint and fresh review when detector configuration changes; activation/preview/assignment reject absent consent, unknown cost and stale fingerprints. Removing the consent checkbox and fingerprint lockout would allow silent external text processing across configuration revisions and contradicts the security contract. Current UI correctly has no detector service configured and performs no external processing. UX simplification should preserve consent/fingerprint semantics rather than delete them.
description:
Trigger: Enabling an external detector in '/workspaces/:ws/guardrails/detectors' or when an admin updates detector configuration.
Impact: ExternalDetectors.tsx:59-98 and DetectorPreview.tsx:57-73 force the workspace developer through a modal legal-consent ceremony ('I approve sending this workspace’s request text to this recipient under these declared conditions.') that binds a 64-char SHA-256 'configuration_fingerprint'. Any platform admin update to the detector's timeout or metadata invalidates the fingerprint and blocks all workspace inference requests ('Review required · requests remain blocked', line 77).
Source: apps/dashboard/app/features/guardrails/ExternalDetectors.tsx:59-98; apps/dashboard/app/features/guardrails/DetectorPreview.tsx:57-73.
notes: 2026-11-05 triage: removing external-detector consent/SHA binding changes a privacy/legal control; needs explicit security/privacy sign-off and a replacement authorization model before code changes.

close_reason: Qiniu account_chat_banned is no longer swallowed: catalog import (vendors/api.rs:1771) and inference rejection mapping (web/inference/common.rs:66) detect the exact Qiniu base + HTTP 403 + account_chat_banned body and return the specific message 'The Qiniu account is not permitted to use chat services (account_chat_banned). Contact Qiniu to restore account access.' The classifier requires exact provider/status/code and the unit test verifies it, while the message contains no private secret. General upstream 4xx/5xx still use bounded generic messages, as intended.
description:
Trigger: Connect Qiniu or send a chat completion request using a Qiniu API key whose account returns HTTP 403 {"error":{"message":"Account is not permitted to use chat services","type":"access_denied_error","code":"account_chat_banned"}}. Also note that GET https://api.qnaigc.com/v1/models returns 200 OK without Authorization but 403 account_chat_banned when Authorization is sent for a chat-restricted key.
Impact: During catalog import (/api/v1/vendors/:id/catalog and /import), Niu discards the upstream error message/code and shows 'The provider rejected the saved API key. Check the key and provider account access.' During chat inference in /generations, Niu shows 'The provider refused this request. Check credential access and regional model availability'. The user never sees the actual upstream error reason ('Account is not permitted to use chat services' / account_chat_banned).
Source: apps/gateway/src/vendors/api.rs:1743-1762, apps/gateway/src/web/inference/.
Acceptance criteria:
- Surface sanitized upstream error messages and error codes (e.g. account_chat_banned: Account is not permitted to use chat services) in catalog discovery, connection check, and inference failure responses.
notes: 2026-11-04: For the canonical Qiniu endpoint and exact HTTP 403 account_chat_banned code, bounded error parsing now returns a fixed account-access remedy in catalog discovery/import and buffered/streaming Chat, preserving inference status and failure attribution without forwarding arbitrary upstream text. Model connection checks return a distinct status; API docs/contracts and SDK types were regenerated, and Chinese UI translation added. Rust classification and HTTP rejection tests, 78 connect/Chat tests, 4 model-check UI tests, dashboard type check, i18n and API contract check passed. Impact: an output limit or filtered/empty terminal result cannot be distinguished from ordinary completion, and a terminal empty result is represented as still waiting. Users lack the information needed to choose a relevant remedy. The observed historical short lists do **not** establish why those specific requests stopped.

Proposed direction: retain and interpret supported finish reasons through live and saved results, separating transport termination, content outcome and unknown evidence. Explain a relevant next step without automatic paid retries or promises that increasing a limit will resolve every case.

In Model access, changing the unsaved model restriction to Block all enables Save. Navigating through Policy preserves the draft and shows a generic unsaved-changes notice, while the access card still says No restrictions from the saved policy. Opening External checks then shows an enabled Save despite no detector changes and no available detectors. That page provides no indication that a model restriction is pending. The shared `Guardrails` component submits the entire `draft` from every section's Save handler. Evidence: E30, actual unsaved navigation and screenshot, plus `features/guardrails/page.tsx` draft lifetime and PUT payload.

Impact: saving from an apparently unrelated section can also commit a hidden workspace-wide model block. The section title and local controls do not describe the effective submission scope. No actual block was enabled: Save was never clicked, and reloading cleared the test draft and disabled Save. The existence of one generic notice on the intermediate Policy page is mitigating evidence, but does not expose the pending changes at the commit point.

Proposed direction: make the commit boundary understandable. Either use explicitly section-scoped drafts and saves, or present a whole-policy editing model with a reviewable pending-change summary and discard path at its save point. Preserve atomic policy validation and revision conflict handling; do not assume separate API writes are required.

Verification: edit section A, visit B without editing it, and establish exactly which changes B's action would commit. Repeat with changes in both sections, invalid hidden input, cancellation, reload and conflict. Users can inspect and discard the affected changes before committing. An existing blocked-request record references a key policy version containing an external input check. Opening that saved version through Guardrails History shows only “1 required check · matches and unavailable services block requests”, alongside Restore this version. The historical input-rule version, by contrast, explicitly names its email-address blocking rule.

Proposed direction: identify the saved check and expose the processing information relevant to the decision. Distinguish historical binding from current configuration/availability; when details are no longer resolvable, say so rather than substituting present-day terms as historical fact. Preserve backend validation and applicable consent. The UI need not display internal fingerprints or raw identifiers.

Imported disposition: New: uncertain key mutation lacks reconciliation and safe recovery

Recheck current code/rendering before implementing; migration is not a new reproduction or authorization for product changes.

**P1 · state/recovery · isolated frontend probes + backend source.** A network rejection leaves an error and re-enables Create/Rotate without checking saved state or warning that the operation may have committed. The backend issues/rotates before constructing the complete response. After response loss, a create retry can create a second credential; a successful rotation may have already invalidated the old secret while the user never received the new one. These consequences are inferred from the implementation path; they were not induced on real keys.

Criterion: distinguish unknown outcome from confirmed failure, prevent harmful retries, and offer a usable recovery path. An intentionally one-time secret is valid; pretending it can always be recovered is not a correction.

Compare TopupFunding's existing uncertain-result handling rather than designing a generic retry loop.

**P1 · actor handoff · G3, J3 · high confidence in inspected entry points; end-to-end provisioning unverified.**

Observation: the account menu switches existing organizations; Organization settings creates workspaces; Users adds a person with a temporary access token; Account balances manages existing companies. Impact: an operator onboarding a new independently funded customer must leave the dashboard and already know the company API. Creating another workspace in the current company is materially different because funds are shared.

Proposed direction: explicitly choose and document console-managed or API-managed company provisioning. Either needs a discoverable operator path through company, owner access, workspace, funds and first usable model. Do not add public self-signup or email invitations merely to imitate another product; those are separate product decisions.

Verification: a new operator can provision an independently funded customer using the supported path, hand off access and verify scope without using a developer's private instructions. Access creation, sign-in and isolation require separately authorized tests.
design: Console-managed customer provisioning is a separate task from Account balances. Reuse company, workspace, scoped owner and password APIs; no public signup or email invitations. Keep independent company funds and configured platform currency. Company, workspace and identity-only owner creation use atomic durable retry receipts. Identity creation issues no session; replay never restores changed/revoked access. Saved setup remains resumable, with tab retry caches disposable. Password configuration read and explicit revision-based reset support owner handoff. Do not label ready until sign-in, scope, supply/access/pricing and funding have been checked.

description:
Source: docs/ux/findings.md (UX-04). Latest reconciliation: docs/ux/continuation-2026-10-21.md, All findings reconciled.

Imported disposition: Active, stronger evidence E02: absent global payment does not gate workspace features

Recheck current code/rendering before implementing; migration is not a new reproduction or authorization for product changes.

**P1 · global prerequisite gate · G3/G6, J3/J4/J8 · user-confirmed requirement; current absence observed.**

Observation: the inspected installation exposes workspace features while Settings → Payments reports online top-ups unavailable and payment gateways remain unconfigured (E05, E10). The earlier finding treated this as a local insufficient-funds recovery problem. The user clarified that valid payment setup is a hard global prerequisite: no workspace feature should become available before it is satisfied.

Impact: the product admits users into workspace workflows before a mandatory installation dependency is ready. Adding a funding link or a local warning would leave the global ordering failure intact. An existing balance, credit allowance or personal upstream key is not an implicit exemption from this setup gate.

Required direction: establish one server-authoritative installation payment-readiness gate shared by all workspaces. Until at least one supported payment method has valid, operational configuration, present an installation setup blocker instead of workspace features. Keep administrator payment setup, authentication, sign-out and necessary recovery/help accessible so the installation can be completed. Ordinary users see the blocker and its responsible operator, not merchant credentials or administration controls. Server-managed gateways may retain their supported configuration procedure; an in-dashboard editor is not inherently required.

Readiness must reflect the gateway's required credentials, merchant activation and required integration checks, not merely a saved configuration record. Apply the gate consistently to direct URLs, existing sessions and workspace API operations, not only navigation visibility. The workspace API key page must let an authorized member copy the full key again after creation, including on a later visit. description:
Trigger and outcome: Niu currently models an operator session as belonging to one organization. An organization is the customer and shared billing boundary; it owns workspaces. A person needs one login for multiple independently funded organizations, each with separate members, access and billing. User confirmed that ordinary signed-in users can create multiple organizations and that the user menu should show the current organization and provide a low-prominence switcher.

Scope: Deliver the complete customer journey and agent/API contracts for self-service organization creation, organization identity and settings, organization and workspace membership administration, switching, and organization billing. A personal user may have their own organization; the organization, not each member individually, pays the Niu customer charges in resale mode. Internal-use provider funding remains separate. Organization owner/admin may manage shared billing within authorized scope; only the authorized member-management role may manage members. Workspace-scoped access must not become organization-wide authority. Platform administration and existing installation-only customer provisioning remain distinct.

Existing state and evidence: at source a1b9e0f41, admin_operators and sessions encode one organization and optional workspace; password credentials, profiles and revocation are attached to operators; account-menu selection changes client state and cannot expand session authority. Existing organization settings show identity and workspaces, and financial views are elsewhere. Existing platform customer provisioning niu-lxs.4 is not self-service organization creation. Partial local uncommitted work exists in crates/storage/migrations/0404_organization_identity.sql, crates/storage/src/account_organization_creation.rs, crates/storage/tests/account_organization_creation.rs, crates/storage/src/lib.rs and apps/dashboard/app/shell/AccountMenu.tsx. Treat it as provisional: inspect, revalidate, revise or replace as necessary. Migration 0404 and the storage creation method are not a complete identity system or public endpoint. Existing independent uncommitted dashboard changes must be preserved. niu-2n1 concurrently changes workspace navigation and proposes moving Members; coordinate against current work and keep organization-scope and workspace-scope permissions clear. niu-ayj.40 tracks broader member acceptance.

Design constraints: preserve existing users, sessions where safe, role grants, Provider ownership, workspace references, balances, request and invoice provenance across migration; never merge identities merely because names or email addresses look alike. Identity, organization memberships and selected session scope must be explicit. Creation must atomically establish ownership and independent zero-funded billing and recover safely from uncertain writes without duplicates; create a usable initial workspace or provide a clear supported setup flow. No customer-funded Provider execution may occur without the normal authorized price/funding admission. Changes of organization membership, role, session, password and revocation must be reflected at every authorization point, including transaction-time checks and concurrent operations. Do not broaden workspace members into organization admins or grant installation authority. Account/profile/password lifecycle must work across memberships without exposing or silently transferring another organization's data. Support loss of access, last-owner protection, concurrent changes and safe recovery. Do not invent an email-invitation delivery capability; make existing supported onboarding and its limitations explicit, or implement a complete authorized invitation flow if needed for the journey.

Switching: only show organizations the signed-in account is authorized to access; the server must resolve and authorize the selected membership, not trust a browser selection. The selected workspace, organization settings, usage, billing, requests and agent context must be scoped consistently. Handle no workspace, revoked access, stale tabs, multiple sessions, reload, direct URLs, failed/lost responses and in-flight requests without cross-organization disclosure or charging. Use durable readable organization slugs in browser paths/query scopes as required by AGENTS.md, while preserving existing API identifiers and authorized legacy routes/bookmarks; a slug is never authorization. Maintain customer-only financial serialization, prevent access to platform procurement and other organizations' balances, and retain historical accounting.

UI and documentation: use existing Niu shell and shadcn primitives. In the user menu show current organization and an accessible switcher without a prominent global header control; preserve selected-state checks and account actions. Make organization management discoverable with organization members, workspaces, settings and billing in the appropriate scope; do not label a workspace as an organization or expose internal IDs. Follow actual mature-product references, ux-review and the repo's browser verification gate, including open menu, keyboard, desktop/intermediate/narrow layouts and errors. Update affected English docs, agent onboarding, SDK/contracts and generated API documentation; mark limitations accurately. Keep niu.io as a resale deployment and maintain the separate self-hosted internal-use policy.
notes:
Handoff for agy: User requested requirements and Beads tracking only; do not interpret this handoff as authorization to change code in this turn. Work remains unfinished. Partial uncommitted storage implementation and a menu label change exist; review them before continuation. The isolated PostgreSQL test previously covered creation replay, changed input, separate identities, zero credit/entries, revoked target and revoked session; it did not validate HTTP, switching, member management, migration of real data, customer charges or financial isolation. Storage clippy and formatting passed. Preserve unrelated concurrent working-tree changes. description: Trigger: app/lib/route-data.ts maintains a single activeRouteLoad and acquireRouteLoadSignal aborts it whenever authority/endpoint/path changes. React Router runs loaders for all matched routes in parallel; today loaders exist only on leaf routes, so the collision is latent. Adding a parent/child loader pair (the normal Data Mode pattern) would abort one of the two reads. Impact: future nested loaders fail intermittently with aborted requests; the current design cannot support nested data routes. Limits: not currently triggered because no route branch has two loaders.

description: Trigger: apps/gateway/src/workspace_events.rs:315 event_delivery_candidates runs every second from apps/gateway/src/resource_events.rs and filters all workspace_event_subscriptions by a JSON enabled flag, authority and an EXISTS over workspace_events, ordered by checked_at,id. description: Trigger: 15 route modules export loader() using loadCriticalRouteEndpoint (app/lib/route-data.ts:136+). On a cold cache it returns {status:'pending', promise} and swallows the promise rejection (void promise.catch), so the router never awaits data and errors never reach the route error boundary. Most pages call useOptionalRouteLoaderData() and ignore the result (customers/page.tsx:32, overview/page.tsx:24); only keys/page.tsx consumes it, and only when status==='ready'. Pages then fetch through useCachedQuery/useEffect, so loader data is unused on cold loads and duplicated on warm loads. Impact: Data Mode is nominal; loaders add latency/code without authoritative data, and loader errors are silent. Limits: no performance trace this pass.
title: P1: Route loaders are deferred snapshots that pages ignore or duplicate

description: Trigger: app/shell/AppLayout.tsx:1170 calls setActiveSessionSnapshot(...) during render, mutating a module-global (app/shell/router-context.ts:68). createRouterContextProvider reads that global, and React Router invokes getContext before each navigation's loaders. On the first load the global is empty, so loaders return unauthenticated/workspace-pending and are not revalidated when the session arrives (AppLayout only revalidates on mutation events, line 1184). Limits: reachable data still loads via component effects, masking the defect.

description:
Trigger: Creating or rotating an API key when localStorage is unavailable/restricted or after any network interruption.
Impact: KeysView.tsx:181-274,384,412-420 and mutation-recovery.ts:25-88 write a pending record to localStorage before sending POST. If a request is interrupted, all future key creation and rotation in the workspace is locked out behind a 'Review key request' modal ('Confirm what happened before creating or rotating another key'), and if the key was created on the server, line 415/418 forces the user to revoke the newly created key ('Revoke this key before creating a new one') to clear the lock!
